baseline_root_cause: The recent migration dropped the compound index idx_tenant_status_name, causing queries to fall back to full table scans and saturating I/O, which led to the latency spike.
reasoning: 1. The git diff shows the index creation line was removed ("--- Note: Compound index idx_tenant_status_name was not recreated on partitions"). 2. After the deployment at 14:04, logs at 14:05 report a changed execution plan: a sequential scan on the items table. 3. Metrics immediately after show db_seq_scans_per_sec jumping from 0 to 120 and disk read throughput soaring, while search latency p95 rises from ~5 ms to >2400 ms. 4. The service code’s MockDatabase simulates missing indexes by incrementing a table_scan_count when the index is absent, confirming that lack of the index forces scans. 5. The combination of missing index → sequential scans → I/O saturation explains the observed latency degradation.

evidence.excerpt: --- Note: Compound index idx_tenant_status_name was not recreated on partitions
WARN [search-service] [db] Query execution plan changed: Seq Scan on items (cost=0.00..45210.00 rows=500000)

suggested_mitigation: Recreate the missing compound index on the partitioned items tables (or adjust the migration to copy the index to each partition) and backfill it; then monitor query plans to ensure index usage returns.
